payload.comment: Profiling stage is clean and internally consistent. PathMNIST (9-class, 28×28 RGB, 3-channel) loaded with full official splits (train 89 996 / val 10 004 / test 7 180), no subsampling, verified MD5 match, and zero blank or duplicate samples. Class imbalance is modest (ratio 1.63) and train/val proportions are nearly identical, indicating no split-level distribution shift. Channel statistics are recorded and reasonable for histology patches. The ambiguity risks (background/debris/mucus overlap, adipose vs. background, smooth muscle vs. stroma, etc.) are inherent to the 28×28 MedMNIST resolution and are correctly flagged as informational rather than pipeline defects. The test-domain note (CRC-VAL-HE-7K, different clinical center) is appropriate context for downstream OOD evaluation. One warning: llm_model_digest is null for qwen3.8 (Ollama), meaning the LLM weights are not checksum-pinned in the run manifest. This weakens full reproducibility of any LLM-assisted step (e.g., augmentation selection, architecture search, or report generation) but does not constitute a deterministic failure. Recommend that a subsequent stage or the run manifest be updated to record a model digest or at minimum a version tag before any LLM-dependent decision is made. No deterministic findings are present, so no stop or revise action is warranted. Proceed to the next stage.
llm_issues: llm_model_digest is null for qwen3.8 (Ollama); model weights are not checksum-pinned, weakening reproducibility of any LLM-assisted downstream step

Ambiguity among visually similar histology classes (background/debris/mucus, adipose/background, smooth muscle/stroma) at 28×28 resolution is a known task limitation; ensure evaluation metrics account for inter-class confusion
Test set originates from a different clinical center (CRC-VAL-HE-7K); OOD aggregate should be computed as the arithmetic mean of per-severity AUROCs, not a pooled-sample AUROC
